news.label: News
news.blurb: Timely items drafted automatically from the source article.
news.description: Auto-drafted from the feed. Timely, disposable, always links to the source.

explainer.label: Fundamentals
explainer.blurb: One concept, properly explained. Still useful next year.
explainer.description: One concept, properly explained, no news hook.

deepdive.label: Deep dive
deepdive.blurb: One thing taken apart: a paper, a system, or something I built.
deepdive.description: One thing taken apart properly — a paper, a system, or something I built and broke.

paper.label: Paper trail
paper.description: One paper, read properly, findings and caveats in plain language.

teardown.label: Teardown
teardown.description: How a technique or system actually works, mechanism first.

postmortem.label: What happened
postmortem.description: An incident or event reconstructed from the record.

notebook.label: Notebook
notebook.description: Something I built, what broke, what it cost.

models.label: Models
models.blurb: New models land constantly and most of the coverage is scorecards. What I care about is what actually changed in how the thing behaves, and whether it changes anything about how you'd build with it.

agents.label: Agents & tooling
agents.description: Agent frameworks, coding tools, MCP, automation.
agents.blurb: Agents are the part of this field where the demo and the production system are furthest apart. This shelf is about the tooling underneath — what it does when nobody is watching the demo.

safety.label: Safety & alignment
safety.blurb: Guardrails matter to me as an operational question, not a philosophical one: if you are responsible for a system, you need to know how much weight a vendor's safety claims can carry in your threat model.

enterprise.label: Enterprise & Microsoft
enterprise.description: Copilot, Azure AI, M365, rollout and adoption.
enterprise.blurb: The gap between an AI feature shipping and an AI feature being rolled out to thirty thousand seats is where I spend my working life. This shelf is about that gap.

mobility.label: Devices & mobility
mobility.description: Intune, Android Enterprise, Apple, EMM, AI on managed devices.
mobility.blurb: Device management is my background, and it is the place where AI stops being an abstraction: models on managed endpoints, policy, compliance, and what a fleet actually allows.

selfhosted.label: Local & self-hosted
selfhosted.description: Ollama, open weights, running things on your own hardware.
selfhosted.blurb: Running models on hardware you control changes the trade-offs completely — cost, privacy, and what happens when the vendor changes the deal. Mostly written from a home lab.

industry.label: Money & industry
industry.blurb: Who owns what, who pays for what, and what that means for anyone building on top of it. Market structure decides which tools still exist in two years.
